To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new learning paradigm, called learning to learn, which allows to transfer prior knowledge to a new learning task.
we can learn to learn from prior knowledge, and that this can be exploited in a life long learning framework.

(a) it is possible to transfer information from a prior knowledge to a target learning problem without any need of supervision, (b) the proposed transfer methods can be used to solve a new learning problem even when only a small amount of training samples are available, (c) the transfer can also exploit the large amount of visual information available on the web, and (d) the obtained transfer methods are able of continuous lifelong learning
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning new concepts from few labeled examples.
the development of learning algorithms able to exploit prior knowledge in order to solve a new learning problem.
the problem of how to learn from experience in an incremental way, taking advantage from past learning to solve new problems with scarce data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methods are capable of learning from very few labeled samples and of exploiting prior knowledge to improve the performance.
we have developed a set of methods which allow to exploit prior knowledge in a principled way.
the proposed methods are able of exploiting any prior knowledge, even if it comes from very different domains and it is not directly related with the target learning problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the goal of learning to learn is to make a machine able to learn from experience and to exploit it in order to solve new tasks.
the proposed solutions allow for a more effective exploitation of the available information and for a better adaptation to a changing and uncertain world.
we propose a new paradigm of machine learning where the learning process can exploit previous experience to improve the performance in a future task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to exploit prior knowledge in a fully automatic way to improve future learning.
it is possible to transfer information from previous learning problems in order to improve the performance of new ones with scarce data.
the exploitation of prior knowledge is a powerful way to reduce the data needed for a reliable learning process, to speed-up learning and to make it more robust.
